articleTitle: A Perspective Spectral Mask for GSC Beamformer in Annoying Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Speech communication plays an important role in human life for transferring necessary information to each other. The numerous speech equipment, such as: hands-free mobile phone, hearing aid, surveillance device, teleconference system, speech recognition are required to have appropriate signal processing algorithm for the designed purpose and recording scenario. Microphone array (MA) beamforming has attracted scholars and researchers for studying the principle working, the advantage of properties of the environment in extracting clean speech while suppressing noise. Generalized sidelobe canceller (GSC) beamformer now commonly implemented in various speech enhancement systems, when there is error in estimation of direction of arrival (DoA) of desired target speaker, the speech leakage occurs in the reference signal due to clean speech will not be block by blocking matrix (BM) completely. Consequently, this factor affects GSC beamfomrer's performance and leads to corrupt speech quality. In this contribution, the authors introduce an effective spectral mask for suppressing the speech leakage to enhance the overall performance. The illustrated method has shown the reducing speech leakage, which often occurs due to the error of estimation of steering vector in the reference signal and increased the speech quality, speech intelligibility and perceptual metric listener, the obtained signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) improved from 6.0 to 10.7 (dB). The numerical result has confirmed the capability of the proposed method in incorporating multi-channel systems and can be used for other purposes of signal processing in MA technology.

articleTitle: Microstrip Antenna with Quasi-Fractal Substructure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: This paper presents the results of numerical simulations of the main electrodynamic characteristics of a planar antenna with a hybrid topology including an open-ended ring microstrip resonator and a disc microstrip resonator with a quasi-fractal internal structure and additional frequency selection. A comprehensive approach was used for numerical simulation, which included the semi-open resonator method and the finite element method (FEM). FEM implementation within the commercial package ANSYS HFFS was used.

articleTitle: Some Expressions for a Circular Cylinder Wave Fields
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: This paper represents a theoretical addition to the first part of the works [1] – [3], concerning the study of the structures of field sources described by the circular cylinder wave functions. The sources of such fields have a multipole nature, so the study of their structures is of theoretical interest. In [1], several possible structures of such multipoles were presented, but the main mathematical expressions were not given in their final form and did not have proper theoretical justification. In this regard, the purpose of this work is to provide the corresponding missing addition.

articleTitle: Radiation Fields of Open Ring Microstrip Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: An approximate rigorous solution on the problem of determination the electromagnetic radiation fields of an open ring microstrip antenna is presented. The solution was carried out using the resonator method and fully takes into account all the geometric parameters of the antenna structure.

articleTitle: On the Problem of Robustness and Resolution of Estimates for the Fractional-Rational Approximation Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: On the basis of numerical modeling, a comparative analysis of accuracy characteristics, stability of estimates of dependence approximation methods and the application of the fractional-rational model was carried out. Quasi-solution, Cauchy, chain fractions methods are under considerations. The Cauchy method [1] provides highly stable and accurate estimates for all considered models, which are superior to the chain fraction method, but inferior to the quasi-solved method. Taking into account the availability of ready-made software, the Cauchy method in interpretation [1] is a very convenient tool for the study of various electrodynamic structures.

articleTitle: Electrodynamic Characteristics of Biconical Dipole with Complex Distributed Surface Impedance and Asymmetric Excitation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: An approximate analytical solution of a problem concerning the radiation of electromagnetic waves from regular and biconical dipoles with constant complex distributed surface impedance and arbitrary point of excitation is obtained. Solution precision is validated by means of acceptable agreement of experimental and numerical results from well-known works. Results of numerical simulation of input characteristics and radiation fields of the dipoles are presented for the cases of its symmetric and asymmetric excitation by a point source.

articleTitle: Electromechanical Properties of the Toroidal Solenoid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The paper is aimed to study of the electrical performances of the solenoids, which are the motion parts of MEMS. The close formulas are given to describe the interconnection of the electrical field power and the mechanical forces in MEMS. The given analytical formulas open the ability to calculate the electrical field components that opens possibility to determine the stored energy in the MEMS constituent parts. The obtained results open ability to model and optimize of parameters of moving parts of MEMS, in particular the actuators, sensors etc.

articleTitle: Remote Determination of Physical and Mechanical Parameters of Thin Flat Non-Contrast Piezoelectric Inclusions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The direct problem of the scattering of horizontal polarization shear waves by thin tunnel planar piezoelectric inclusions of low contrast has been investigated. Analytical formulas for wave fields of the displacements in an elastic medium were obtained. An effective algorithm for determining the physical and mechanical parameters of such inclusions based on the data of shear wave scattering in the far zone is proposed.

articleTitle: Improved Cylindrical Antenna Model for Assesment of Influence of the EM field on a Human Body
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The Human Body Communication (HBC) approach is used to size up the electromagnetic (EM) field impact on the human body within the 4G operator frequencies. The analysis foresees the application of the equivalent cylindrical monopole antenna concept, which is applied to the standing human body. The close formulas, which allow to determine the EM field inside and outside antenna are given. The numerical data related to study of incident axial current in the cylindrical approach are examined. The obtained data open the perspective to study the values of the specific absorption rate (SAR) involving the realistic physical model of the human body.

articleTitle: Analytical Solution of Linear Antenna Synthesis Problems According to Given Amplitude Directivity Pattern at the Least Squares Deviation for the Phase of Solution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: An advanced method of constructing an analytical-numerical solution of the nonlinear antenna synthesis problem based on a given amplitude directivity pattern is considered. Using the method of least squares, the case of obtaining an approximate analytical solution of the problem of non-convex minimization of functional for the case of isometric operator of direct problem is presented. Numerical results are given that confirm the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Determining the Zone of Successful Interaction in RFID Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Methodical aspects of determining the zone of successful interaction between RFID tags and readers used to solve problems of automatic identification and spatial localization of objects in enclosed spaces are considered. The proposed method identifies the probabilistic traits associated with the effective interaction zone between RFID tags and the reader. This facilitates a more strategic placement of sensitive elements within readers and the selection of tag detection thresholds based on predetermined probability distributions for the instability of the informative parameter's initial, controlled, and residual values. The suggested mathematical model for the operation of the primary measuring transducer aligns well with experimental evaluations. The variance between theoretical and experimental values of the informative parameter is within a 5% margin. The considered method makes it possible to determine zones of successful interaction between the tag and the reader.

articleTitle: Reactive Impedance of Linear Radiator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The theorem about the fluctuating power is used for the analysis of the discussion connected with the method of induced emf and similar methods.

articleTitle: On the Modeling of Acoustic Fields in a Half Space with Acoustically Hard Inclusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The initial boundary value problem for the homogeneous wave equation is considered in a three-dimensional half space containing an inclusion. The plane forming the boundary of the half space is treated as ‘acoustically soft’, while the boundary of the inclusion is ‘acoustically hard’ Lipschitz surface. The solution to the problem is formulated as a modified single layer wave potential which vanishes at the boundary of the half space due to a special kernel. To determine the unknown density of the potential, a time domain boundary integral equation (TDBIE) of the second kind is derived. By applying the Laguerre transform, the TDBIE is reduced to a sequence of boundary integral equations (BIEs) that are solved only on the surface of the inclusion. Using the standard boundary element method (BEM), the Laguerre coefficients of the desired solution are computed by sequentially solving these BIEs. Numerical experiments for model problems demonstrate the efficiency of combining the Laguerre transform with BEM. The calculation of approximate solutions is much faster than using the wave double layer potential or the Kirchhoff formula. Additionally, error analysis and estimated order of convergence confirm the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Expectation Maximum Algorithm - Based Enhanced Speech Enhancement by Using Microphone Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Microphone array (MA) technology use the designed MA configuration, the preferred direction of arrival of interest useful signal, the priori information about environmental properties, the characteristics of surrounding noise, the distribution of mounted microphones to achieve an optimum filter's coefficient. Consequently, the multi-channel signal processing method has an important role in realistic performance of almost acoustic instruments. However, in the annoying recording scenario, the evaluation often decreased, because of the complex challenging of computing the time - varying variance of received signals in adverse recording situation for forming steered beampattern. In this paper, the author suggests using the expectation maximum (EM) algorithm to exactly compute the variance of speech/noise, which according to the complex Gaussian mixture model in adverse environments, to form a Wiener filter. The conducted experiment in real-life situations has confirmed the effectiveness of the author's proposed technique both in suppressing unwanted noise and preserving the original clean speech data. This approach increased the speech quality, speech intelligibility and perceptual metric listener in the term of signal-to-noise (SNR) ratio from 6.4 dB to 14.4 dB and reduced the speech distortion to 8.0 dB in comparison with the single-channel method. This direction approach can be integrated into multi-channel array signals to solve other realistic complicated problems.

articleTitle: Analysis of Dynamic Displacements in a Bimaterial with a Torsion Crack
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The problem of time-harmonic torsional loading of a penny-shaped crack in an elastic bimaterial of two perfectly contacted half-spaces is considered. The solutions for the dynamic displacements in the solid body were obtained using the boundary integral equations (BIEs) method. The dependences of dynamic displacements in the bimaterial on the frequency of the applied load, the stiffness ratio of the body materials, and the location of the signal observation points were calculated and analyzed.

articleTitle: Assessment of the EM Radiation Level in Tbilisi School Locations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The goal of the presented research is to study the electromagnetic (EM) background in the selected school areas of the city Tbilisi (Georgia). Based on the results obtained by the direct measurements, the electromagnetic field values were marked on the geographical map of Tbilisi in accordance with the school locations and hot spots were highlighted. i.e., based on the measured values, an EM pollution map is created. It was determined whether the EM field values comply with the existing safety limits.

articleTitle: Polarization and Frequency Selective Characteristics of a Chiral Metasurface Consisting of Periodically Arranged Square Dielectric Helices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The paper concerns the polarization and frequency-selective characteristics of a chiral metasurface consisting of periodically arranged square dielectric helices. The study focuses on the efficient manipulation of optical properties such as amplitude, phase, polarization, chirality, and anisotropy, using all-dielectric nanostructures with high permittivity.

articleTitle: Exponential and Rational Models for Radar Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Time and frequency properties of the signal of a radar system are investigated. The structures of transmitter and receiver are described. The exponential and rational models are used in the time domain and in domain of Discrete Fourier Transform. Modulated, no modulated and noise signals are examined. Several approaches to spectral analysis are compared. Some improvements for finding eigen frequencies are proposed.

articleTitle: Solution of 3D Electromagnetic Diffraction Problem by PEC Circular Double Disks Using the Method of Auxiliary Sources
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the electromagnetic diffraction characteristics of 3D perfect electric conductor (PEC) parallel circular double disks illuminated by a Hertzian dipole with arbitrary polarization. The problem is solved by applying the method of auxiliary sources (MAS), which simplifies complex electromagnetic field problems by utilizing auxiliary sources to represent the scattered fields. The numerical results, obtained by developing a MATLAB-based simulation package, examine the frequency characteristics and field distributions for different planes. This study provides insights into resonant characteristics and diffraction patterns, which have significant implications for optimizing and designing resonators used in applications such as radar, antenna and satellite communication systems.

articleTitle: Combined Dipole-Slot Radiating Structures with Parasitic Impedance Dipoles as Functional Elements of Antennas and Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Mathematical models and algorithms for calculating the electrodynamic characteristics of multi-element slotted waveguide antennas and antenna arrays, the functional elements of which are combined dipole-slot radiating structures with parasitic impedance dipoles, have been construct using the generalized method of induced electro-magnetomotive forces. The electrodynamic characteristics of a combined structure consisting of a radiating slot in the wall of a rectangular waveguide and parasitic impedance dipole placed above it were investigated. The geometric and electrophysical parameters of the radiating structure are defined, which ensure the maximum achievable value of the directivity for such a dipole-slot radiator or realize the radiator with the same width of the radiation pattern in E- and H-planes.

articleTitle: Dynamic Strength of an Elastic Matrix with a Partially Healed Crack
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The problem of the incidence of a plane time-harmonic wave on a healed crack by filling it with an injection material in an elastic matrix is considered. The problem is reduced to solving a two-dimensional boundary integral equation with respect to the unknown function of the opening of the opposite surfaces of the defect. The frequency dependencies of the dynamic stress intensity factor on the stiffness ratio of the composite materials, the thickness of the defect, and the dimensions of the crack filler region are calculated and analyzed.

articleTitle: Reflective Properties of a Thin Wire Substrate-Like Metagrating
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: In this study, a hybrid solution of the problem of scattering of a plane electromagnetic wave oblique incident on a wire metagrating located on infinite dielectric layer backed by a conducting background is obtained. The metagrating is an infinite set of identical thin infinitely long metal cylindrical wires of circular cross section periodically located on the interface between free space and top of the dielectric layer. The solution of the above problem has obtained basing on the approaches proposed by J.R. Wait and D. Hill for structures containing thin wire gratings. Microwave approximations for amplitudes of the scattered electric field component and total reflection coefficient from the surface of the structure under consideration have obtained. The dependence of the magnitude and phase of the reflection coefficient on the angles of incidence have analyzed. The analytical approximations have been verified by numerical simulations using a commercial electromagnetic software at microwave frequencies.

articleTitle: Variance of Desired Speaker Estimation Based Speech Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Microphone array (MA) beamforming plays an essential role in numerous speech applications. The existence of ambient noise, third-party talker, incoherent background noise, diffuse noise field, adverse room acoustics, the imperfectly determined environmental factors degenerate the speech quality and speech intelligibility. Digital signal processing is a vital important component in a speech enhancement (SE) system for suppressing surrounding noise while saving the original clean speech data. SE incorporates a priori spatial information of MA's distribution with beamforming, the properties of recording scenarios to an appropriate spatial filter. Minimum Variance Distortionless Response (MVDR) beamforming is one of the most effective techniques of obtaining the desired target speaker at a certain direction without speech distortion and removing total noise power. However, due to many reasons, such as: the different MA sensitivities, the MA mismatch, the error of the direction of arrival of interest signal, the overall MVDR beamformer's performance degraded. In this conference paper, the author proposed a gain function, which is based on the assumption about presence/absence of speech component to improve the MVDR's beamformer performance in noisy realistic situations. The numerical results show the capability of the suggested technique in increasing the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) from 7.3 dB to 8.8 dB and reducing the speech distortion to 11.0 dB.

articleTitle: Optimization Approach to Modification of Characteristics of Bragg Structure Based on Parametric Weighting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Weight processing of the values of reflection coefficients from the interfaces of layers of a Bragg-type structure reducing the side lobe level in the passband of the reflection frequency response is considered. To ensure a reduction of the level of side lobes in the Bragg structure at a fixed width of the Bragg reflection, a technology based on optimization of the objective function containing samples of the frequency response in the passband has been developed. The conditions for the dielectric constant values exceeding unity and not decreasing the reflection level in the reflection frequency band are shown. The results of using the Taylor window, which has found application in modern radar and antenna technology, are presented.

articleTitle: Mathematical Model for Attenuated Infrasound Wave Propagation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The paper presents a comprehensive mathematical model for simulating the propagation and attenuation of infrasound waves within the atmosphere. This framework leverages a modular approach, integrating atmospheric, infrasound attenuation, and infrasound waveform propagation models.

articleTitle: Monomode Waveguide Resonators for Microwave and Optical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: We present the results of model synthesis of two open waveguide resonators with a single dominant eigen oscillation in a frequency band spanning one octave. The first resonator is constructed as a section of a regular plane-parallel (or rectangular) waveguide bounded by two identical rectangular grooves in the side wall. The second one is made using the same principle but for a waveguiding defect in a photonic crystal and can be used for applications in the infrared wavelength range. Estimates for the frequencies and quality factors of the working oscillations are obtained.

articleTitle: Tilted Cone-Enhanced Ultrawideband Monopole-Slot Radiators in Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The study presents several configurations of antenna arrays based on a modified ultrawideband combined monopole-slot radiator, ultrawideband analog of the Clavin radiator. The modification involves tilting the cones within the structure, enhancing the interaction between the ultrawideband slot and the short-circuited monopoles. This adjustment enables effective radiation at lower frequencies and improves the impedance matching across a broad frequency range. The paper provides an analysis of time-domain responses and directivity patterns at various angles for different antenna array configurations, highlighting the impact of the tilted cone design.

articleTitle: Assessment of Electromagnetic Field Exposure to Humans at 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi Frequency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The purpose of the presented research is to investigate the thermal effects caused by electromagnetic field (EMF) exposure to humans at 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi frequency using numerical simulations. The finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method-based simulation software FDTDLab was used for the numerical calculations. Based on EM and thermal simulations, we estimated the EMF exposure to human bodies (female and child) in terms of the specific absorption rate (SAR) and the temperature rise caused by the EMF absorption in body tissues and the resultant dielectric heating. In particular, we determined 1g and 10g mass-averaged SAR, the whole-body averaged SAR, and temperature rise values inside the human whole-body and body parts. The compliance of the results with the safety limits was also investigated according to international standards related to SAR and temperature rise.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis of Metalens Characteristics: Simulation Results
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The paper presents the results of modeling linear metalenses based on split-ring resonators and double Möbius strips of different diameters using Ansys HFSS software. The study examined the distribution of the magnetic field (H-field) and analyzed the efficiency of the metalenses in different frequency ranges with variable focal distances. It was found that the investigated metalenses can act as either focusing or dispersing, depending on the radiation frequency and the distance to the lens surface. It was shown that at a frequency of 3.9 GHz, the Möbius strips provide a focal distance four times shorter (10 mm) compared to classical meta-elements in the form of split-ring resonators (40 mm). This effect can lead to a significant reduction in the size of microwave bridges and splitters. The obtained results demonstrate the promise of using the proposed metalens designs in the development of compact and highly efficient radio systems.

articleTitle: Mathematical Modeling of Wave Diffraction on a Conical Grating with Semitransparent Strips
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The rigorous diffraction boundary problem for a semitransparent slotted semi-infinite cone is considered. Slots are periodically cut along its generatrices from the cone tip. The source field is assumed to be monochromatic. The solution method uses the Kontorovich-Lebedev integral transform method and the singular integral equation (SIE) one. The SIE is obtained for a slotted semitransparent cone boundary problem and a magnetic dipole excitation. For the cone of the transparency parameter limiting value and a longitudinal slot field distribution patterns are given. The slot influence on the field behavior at the conical tip is studied.

articleTitle: On the Synthesis of a Matching-Reflecting Multilayer Dielectric Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: A technology to synthesize multilayer dielectric structures in a waveguide with matching in the frequency band of the main signal and reflection of the second harmonic in the frequency band has been developed. To calculate the characteristics, the Brillouin concept for waves in a waveguide is used. The structure contains 13 layers. The middle 3 layers provide the properties of a Bragg mirror, and the surrounding structures serve to match the structure with the hollow waveguide on both sides. The poles and zeros of the frequency response of the structure are analyzed.

articleTitle: Analytical Prediction of Magnetic Field Shielding for Multilayer Thin Sheets Excited by Loop Sources
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: This paper presents an analytical method for calculating the near-field magnetic shielding effectiveness of two- and three-layer thin sheets. Using the vector wave equation and boundary conditions, the method calculates the shielding effectiveness, with integrals evaluated both numerically and analytically. This approach is validated by experimental data from Moser's research and numerical modelling based on low-frequency Method of Moments. The main value of this study lies in the ability to predict the shielding effectiveness of multilayer sheets under known material properties, which helps to determine the optimum thicknesses of layers.

articleTitle: Determination of the Location of the Radiation Source
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The paper explores the use of the trilateration method (a distance-difference measurement technique) to determine the location of a radiation source. The analysis focuses on a scenario where signals emitted by a single source are received by three spatially separated receivers, positioned at the vertices of a triangle. The relative time delays of the received signals are used to calculate the coordinates of the source. The accuracy of this localization method depends on factors such as the precision in measuring the signal arrival times at the receivers and the accuracy in determining the coordinates of the receivers. To estimate the inaccuracy of the transmitter's position we rely on numerical examples. The paper presents the results of numerical estimations that assess the feasibility of using the trilateration approach to meet practical requirements.

articleTitle: Measuring the Line Density of Plasma Electrons by Three-Probe Microwave Interferometry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: In this paper, a three-probe microwave interference method for measuring the line density of plasma electrons is presented. The problem of phase ambiguity is solved by measuring changes in the line electron density and starting the measurement process before plasma discharge initiation. It is shown that ignoring that the interprobe distances are not necessarily equal to their setting values may be responsible for a marked error, and a simple technique for electrical measurements of the actual interprobe distances is presented.

articleTitle: Some Expressions for Sectoral and Tesseral Spherical Wave Fields
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: This paper represents a theoretical addition to the third part of the works [1] – [3], concerning the study the multipole sources structures of the sectoral and tesseral wave fields. The main expressions from the work [3] are justified and reduced to their final form. Some recurrence formulas are given. It is shown that the operators connecting the considered functions with a zero-order function represents the eigen-operators of spherical harmonic polynomials.

articleTitle: Synthesis of TL Resonators with 3λ/4-Mode Oscillations for Bandpass Filters with Multiple Transmission Zeros
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: In this report, a stepped-impedance resonator (SIR) is synthesized, operating at the second resonant frequency <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\omega_{02}$</tex>, corresponding to oscillations <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3\lambda/4$</tex>. It has two anti-resonant frequencies <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\omega_{\mathrm{p}1}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\omega_{\text{p2}}$</tex> close to each other, which are equidistant relative to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\omega_{02}$</tex>. The antiresonant frequencies of the transmission line (TL) resonator are the poles of its input admittance. Using this resonator in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex>-order bandpass filter (BPF) results in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2N$</tex> tunable transmission zeros (TZ) without cross and mixed couplings. These TZs represent <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> pairs, in each of which these frequencies are located equidistantly. The specified pattern of TZ placement makes it possible to implement BPF with quasi-elliptic and elliptic transfer functions. Moreover, the use of synthesized SIR in the BPF allows to allows to realize equidistant TZ pairs of higher degree, which leads to increased BPF selectivity. The length of the synthesized SIR with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3\lambda/4$</tex> oscillation, is 3 times longer than quarter-wave resonators. This makes it possible to use these resonators at very high frequencies, including millimeter range. The fourth-order BPF prototype is considered.

articleTitle: Influence of Aperture Angle of Finite Size Corner Antenna on its Directional and Band Properties
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The fast-active software has been developed based on the solution of the three-dimensional vector problem of diffraction of the dipole field on a finite-size corner within the framework of the method of uniform geometric diffraction theory. This software has been used for determining the maximum achievable coefficients of directivity in the direction of the normal to the corner aperture, and the appropriate sizes and shapes of the corner's reflector along with the distance between it and dipole. It has been investigated the calculated dependencies of the directivity, corresponding radiation resistance and radiation patterns of corner antennas with optimal parameters at different aperture angles, excited by a half-wave dipole parallel to the internal edge of the corner, in the operating band of wavelengths from four to fourteen cm. The reliability of the obtained results is confirmed by their comparison with the results of the FEKO program calculation.

articleTitle: Optimization of Single-Channel Moving Target Indication Filters Using Pulse Repetition Interval Staggered
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The rapid development of various types of air vehicles, from small unmanned aerial vehicles to supersonic missiles, puts forward increased requirements for radar developers to cover an expanded range of speeds of 10–3000 m/s, especially in multi-target environments. Analytical dependencies for calculating the parameters for the pulse repetition interval staggered law of the pulse signal are proposed. We are using them to increase the efficiency of single-channel filters for moving target indication. A method for optimizing a signal-filter pair to determine the parameters of the signal is proposed. This method is applied to the most common single-channel optimal Doppler filters synthesized according to various quality criteria.

articleTitle: A Mathematical Model Creation for Vibration Propagation in a Plate Based on the Concept of a Longitudinally Moving One-Dimensional Body
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: A mathematical model has been developed to describe the impact of the mechanical characteristics of plate materials on oscillation frequency. The construction of this model utilizes the fundamental concept of wave motion in longitudinally moving one-dimensional bodies and the Van der Pol method. The study examines the propagation of oscillations in both resonant and non-resonant cases for plates with varying elastic properties. The findings from this research can be applied to the optimization and configuration of electronic components in devices and equipment.

articleTitle: Investigation of Plasmon Resonances in Silver Concentric Nanoshell (“Nanomatryushka”)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: In this paper the resonance characteristics of silver concentric symmetrical nanostructure or “nanomatryushka” are comprehensively investigated. A silver nanowire with double symmetrical layer is considered as the basic structure. The obtained characteristics were compared with the optical properties of a standard isolated nanowire. All possible plasmon resonance modes of the concentric silver structure are detected. The all bonding and antibonding combinations of the plasmons are investigated as the result of the hybridization for concentric nanostructure.

articleTitle: Design of Bandpass Filters with High Mode 5λ/4 Oscillations and Equidistant Transmission Zeros Pairs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The report presents a design sequence of a third-order bandpass filter (BPF) based on parallel resonators and J-inverters. This filter is based on synthesized transmission line (TL) resonators with special properties. These resonators provide the filter with six transmission zeros (TZ) resulting in increased BPF selectivity. At the same time, the cross or mixed couplings are not used in this filter. Moreover, these TZs are three equidistant pairs. Each TL resonator provides an adjustable pair of equidistant TZs. The TL resonators are stepped impedance resonators (SIR) with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5\lambda/4$</tex> oscillation, whose length is 5 times longer than the quarter-wave resonator. This makes it possible to use these resonators at very high frequencies, including the millimeter range. The design sequence discussed, including established patterns, can be used for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex>-order BPFs with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2N$</tex> adjustable TZs. The prototype of a third-order BPF with six TZs is considered.

articleTitle: Improved Algorithm for Approximate Solution of Integral Equations of Diffraction Problems on Periodic Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: In the proposed algorithm, functions that do not have continuous derivatives are extracted from the kernels of integral expressions. Interpolation quadrature formulas are proposed for calculating integrals from these functions. These formulas are precise for polynomials whose degree is less than the number of interpolation points. The accuracy of application of these formulas for a class of functions whose derivatives of degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> is Hölder continuous was evaluated.

articleTitle: Some Expressions for Zonal Spherical Wave Fields. Linear Multipole
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: This paper represents a theoretical addition to the second part of the works [1] – [3], concerning the study of the field sources structure described by zonal spherical wave functions. It is shown that the operator connecting the fields under consideration with the monopole field is the eigen-operator of the spherical harmonic polynomial. Some recurrence formulas are given. It is shown that the linear multipole proposed in [2] can be obtained in a slightly different way. New values of monopole amplitudes are found for which the linear multipole more accurately describes the field under consideration. Some generalization for a linear multipole is presented.

articleTitle: The Solution of the Direct Problem on the Propagation of Millimiter Waves in Liquid Foam Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The work is devoted to the study reflection of electromagnetic waves in the millimeter range from liquid foam structures. This topic is very complex, because liquid foam structure is not stable, it constantly disintegrates within a short time. So, it requires a very short time of measurements and processing of data. The multi-frequency method of measurement and fast Fourier transformation is used. The method is implemented on the set of devices for measurements and calculations in the frequency range 38 – 52 GHz. The considered method makes it possible to separately analyze the reflection coefficients from the upper and lower faces of the investigated foam structure. Foam generator made it possible to obtain structures 40 mm thick with quasi-one-dimensional inhomogeneities in the form of bubbles. The obtained results indicate very low reflectance values (less then −42 dB for 10 minutes of foam existence), of the investigated foam structure. The results confirm the possibility of foam to use it in the range of millimeter waves for the tasks of masking metal objects.

articleTitle: Mathematical Modelling of EM Wave Scattering from Electrically Narrow Strip and Coplanar Strip Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Basic mathematical models of linear polarized electromagnetic waves' scattering from electrically conductive zero-thickness strips' system are presented. Linear polarized electromagnetic waves' scattering from alone conductive zero-thickness strip is studied in detail. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E$</tex>-polarized wave scattering's model is presented as the first kind log-singular integral equation. The second mathematical model is presented by the Cauchy's type singular integral equation of the first kind with two conditions. It deals with the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${H}$</tex>-polarized wave scattering from single electrically conductive strip. Both mathematical models are used to create correct asymptotical models of electromagnetic wave's scattering from eelectrically narrow strip. In that important case electromagnetic wave scattering's solutions are obtained in an analytical and explicit form. For more essential case of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${E}$</tex>-polarized wave's scattering from alone impedance strip some numerical experiments are realized. In particular, influence of impedance parameter on the scattering problem's solution is studied

articleTitle: Analytical Modeling and Analysis of Airy Pulse Interaction with a Dynamic Boundary
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: This paper focuses on the study, analysis, and simulation modeling of the Airy pulse in a nonstationary inhomogeneous medium characterized by the presence of a flat moving boundary. The effects of the moving boundary on the frequency and amplitude of the Airy pulse are examined, and an analytical analysis of the transient processes involved in this interaction is performed.

articleTitle: Comparison of Radiation Characteristics of a Dipole with a Square Screen depending on their Distance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The high-speed computing programs have been developed, based on an asymptotic 3D solution of the problem of radiation diffraction from a resonant half-wave dipole located parallel to a perfectly conducting rectangular screen. There are calculated directive gain, radiation resistance and the Back to Front Ratio as the functions of the square screen side size <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> and the distance between the dipole and the screen <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h$</tex>, which have been varied within two and one resonant wavelengths correspondingly. The first two resonant positions of the dipole <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h$</tex> and the corresponding dimensions of the square screen <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> has been determined, at which the maximum directive gain in the normal direction to the screen is increased by 31 and 51 percent relatively to the efficiency of a dipole with an infinite screen. For these two resonant dipole positions the optimization of the antenna by the minimal Back to Front Ratio has been made by choosing the suitable screen's sides ratio from a given range of values at fixed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>. Finally, the optimal antenna geometric parameters have been retrieved which provide the maximum achievable directive gain forward and minimal Back to Front Ratio. The radiation patterns for such antennas have been calculated and analyzed.

articleTitle: Altering Magnetic Permeability of a Material Supplemented with Chaotically Embedded Particles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: We apply an analytical-numerical method to solve the scattering problem on a set of particles chaotically embedded into a homogeneous material. The assumption on particle smallness allows for the asymptotic approach. Solution's analytical part consists in the derivation of a closed formula for a system of linear algebraic equations (SLAE) with respect to unknown auxiliary function values. Solving this SLAE numerically, we obtain both the solution to the initial scattering problem and an explicit formula for the magnetic permeability in the resulting inhomogeneous material. Numerical experiments prove the possibility of significantly changing magnetic permeability distribution - in contrast to the cases of embedding particles regularly or by some patterns. With an explicit formula available, we can also solve the inverse problem via heuristic algorithms.

articleTitle: Study of the Processes of Magnetization Reversal and Pinning of Domain Walls in Cobalt Nanowires Polarized in an Epoxy Matrix
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The processes of NMR signal amplification and transverse relaxation time T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> reduction, as well as domain wall pinning force reduction during magnetization reversal of a sample with cobalt nanowires oriented in an external magnetic field in an epoxy matrix, were studied. Two complementary methods were used for this purpose - the microscopic spin echo NMR method using an additional magnetic video-pulse and the macroscopic resonant RF magnetometry method. These methods provide information on the coercive force of cobalt nanowires, domain wall pinning force, and their anisotropy depending on the outer magnetic field direction relative to the nanowire magnetization. This information can be useful for improving the technology of cobalt nanowire production for their practical use in sensors, memory devices, permanent magnets that do not contain rare earth elements, and other applications.

articleTitle: On the Integral Equations for the Current in the Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Issues of integral equations' application for analysis of current distribution and calculation of electrical characteristics of different types of antennas are considered. The method of calculating the total current and input impedance of a linear radiator is offered. The results are generalized to the case of a structure of several radiators. The possibilities of their application to curvilinear and microstrip radiators have been considered.

articleTitle: Spectral Boundary Integral Equation Methods for Electromagnetic Research with Different Geometrical Configurations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Electromagnetic research with different geometrical configurations requires application of numerical simulation methods. In most of cases geometry of scatterers is simple, including circles or ellipses. Such shapes may be investigated by generalized Mie theory. However, investigation of other shapes requires the application of other methods. While domain discretization methods such as Finite Difference Time Domain method as we as Finite Element Method require the discretization of whole space, Boundary Integral Equation methods including classical Boundary Element Method require discretization of boundaries. Thus, conformal mapping approach to generate the parametrization of boundaries in combination with spectral Boundary Integral Equation method improved by analytical regularization based on singularity subtraction technique enhanced by Fast Fourier Transform is ideal to solve boundary value problem on polygonal structures with various configurations, while multiple multipole program and Method of Auxiliary Sources are also applicable to solve similar problems. Rewire of structures and corresponding techniques to make electromagnetic research on them is done in this work. Summary of techniques is used to solve full three-dimensional problem generating three-dimensional analog of specified two-dimensional Spectral Boundary Integral Equation method.

articleTitle: Solving Linear Inverse Problems via Criterion of Minimum Extent
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 29th International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: A new approach based on the minimum-extent criterion is proposed for solving linear inverse problems. The minimum-extent criterion requires minimizing the extent of the function used to solve the inverse problem. The proposed approach combines the requirements to minimize both the extent of the residual of the problem solution and the extent of some function related to the problem solution. This approach generalizes known approaches based on the criteria of least squares, least absolute deviation, meridian filtering, and myriad filtering. Additionally, it allows tuning to a noise environment with a symmetric noise distribution in the presence of anomalous values. The approach's performance is demonstrated numerically by solving the inverse problem of restoring a set of dipole sources from computer-simulated near-field data distorted by noise and outliers.
